Definition: a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined):--about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with. In composition it retains many of these applications, and frequently denotes opposition, distribution, or intensity.
BiblicalUsage: This little word does heavy work, and almost every time it appears it is setting the measure of something: according to God's purpose, according to the counsel of His will, according to the Scriptures, and even greeting friends by name, each one on his own account. It tells me whose standard counts and whose story I am living inside. Read it slowly and the sentence changes, because who sets the measure decides what the words mean.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the hinge of the gospel, because everything hangs on whether things happen according to God or according to me. I hold that Romans 8:28 is only good news if the purpose is His, and the counsel is His, and the Scriptures are His, and my part is to trust the measure He has set.
